parameters: Scale 0 3 5 7 10. Four lines of equal length. The second half repeats the first half a fifth lower
link_to_the_reference_composers: Bartók's base material. The lonely melody of Melody in the Mist is in this style

parameters: Citera (zither), cimbalom (hammered strings), duda (bagpipe), tárogató (reed), kaval (flute), doromb (jaw harp), tekerő (hurdy-gurdy)
link_to_the_reference_composers: Possible colours for the orchestra. Bartók imitates the bagpipe in Musettes

parameters: Free rhythm. Many ornaments. The singer improvises on a more or less fixed pattern that usually descends. The long notes are the fourth or the fifth above the lowest note
link_to_the_reference_composers: Bartók found it in 1912. He found related types in Ukraine, Albania, Algeria, the Middle East, and North India, and he linked it to the maqam system. Thus the long song connects three of the four selected traditions

parameters: Groups of 2 and 3 at fast tempo: 2+2+3; 2+2+2+3; 3+2+2; 2+3
link_to_the_reference_composers: Bartók's "Bulgarian rhythm": String Quartet No. 5, Mikrokosmos

item: Flute melody heard from far away at night
parameters: Dorian mode. Narrow range. The melody grows out of repeated notes

item: Many callers who do not agree in time
parameters: About 4 o'clock at night. First one voice, then tens of voices. At one moment all hold one note: a major chord. Then silence, a cock, a dog, dawn
link_to_the_reference_composers: Corigliano heard it and wrote the Nocturne of the String Quartet and Symphony No. 2

tradition: Call to prayer by time of day
item: A different maqam for each of the five calls
parameters: The maqam agrees with the time of day
link_to_the_reference_composers: A model for modes that change with the hours. This is sacred music: the new work must not imitate the call itself

item: Melody type and method of improvisation
parameters: No fixed metre. The maqam gives the tonic, the dominant note, and the notes to emphasize. Scales have 7 notes with microtones. Notation rounds them to quarter-tones; the frequent half-flat notes are E, B, and A. The melody starts low, goes up by stages to a climax, then comes down. Violin, nay, qanun, and clarinet can play the intervals
link_to_the_reference_composers: Bartók linked the Romanian long song to the maqam system. Corigliano uses quarter-tones for expression

item: Ragas for the hours of the night
parameters: Yaman: first quarter of the night (about 21:00 to 24:00). Bageshri: middle of the night. Malkauns: 24:00 to 03:00. Darbari Kanada: midnight, deep in the night. The opening (alap) has no metre, is improvised above a drone, and starts slowly. In one method the notes come one at a time, and the first note in a new octave is a strong event. Then a pulse starts (jor), then the tempo becomes fast (jhala)
link_to_the_reference_composers: Same idea as night music: a slow, free line above a still background. Same process as Schoenberg's themes that go up in register

item: Music for a full night in three stages
parameters: The mode (pathet) changes through the night. Slendro: nem, then sanga, then manyura. Pelog: lima, then nem, then barang. Each pathet has its cadence. Slendro nem: 6 5 3 2. Sanga: 2 1 6 5. Manyura: 3 2 1 6
link_to_the_reference_composers: A model for a large form that follows the hours of the night

item: Gongs that mark nested cycles of time
parameters: Lancaran: a cycle of 16 beats. The large gong sounds 1 time. The kenong divides the cycle into 4. The kempul divides each of these parts into 2. The ketuk divides again into 2. Groups of 4 are most frequent at all levels
link_to_the_reference_composers: A fixed slow cycle below free layers: a way to show time in the night music

item: Two instruments tuned a small interval apart
parameters: The pair makes beats. The speed of the beats is the same for all notes in all registers
link_to_the_reference_composers: Same idea as Bartók's badly tuned pair of bagpipes (Musettes) and Corigliano's two pianos a quarter-tone apart: a shimmer

item: Cluster chords of the mouth organ (shō)
parameters: The shō has 17 bamboo pipes with free reeds; 15 of them sound. The reeds sound when the player breathes in and breathes out, thus the sound does not stop. The standard chords have 5 or 6 notes and are held with a slow change
link_to_the_reference_composers: Cluster harmony as a still background, much older than Bartók. The accordion is a free-reed instrument of the same family

parameters: One phrase = one breath. Silence (ma) is part of the music. Pitch bends, air noise
link_to_the_reference_composers: A model for a lonely melody with silence

item: Music for a ceremony that continues through the night
parameters: Cycles of 12 or 48 pulses. Two or more interlocked parts. The listener hears melodies that no single player plays
link_to_the_reference_composers: Layers that make new patterns together

parameters: 12 pulses: 2 2 1 2 2 2 1. All other parts align to the bell
link_to_the_reference_composers: A fixed cycle below free layers

parameters: Chords A minor, G, F, E. Cycle of 12 beats with accents on 3, 6, 8, 10, 12 (soleá)
link_to_the_reference_composers: Night as a subject in Spanish music (Falla)

item: Rocking song for a child at night
parameters: Small range. Falling minor third. Slow 6/8 or 2/4. Many repeats
link_to_the_reference_composers: Bartók: Lullaby from Village Scenes is on the night music list

parameters: Fire-bellied toad (Bombina bombina), cicada, birds; tufted titmouse, wood thrush
link_to_the_reference_composers: The Night's Music; Piano Concerto No. 3
